sentences.text: Gobipteryx was approximately the size of a partridge, with a skull length of 45 millimeters.
This bird possessed a toothless beak formed by fused premaxillae bones.
The vertebral column consisted of at least 19 presacral vertebrae, with the last six being dorsals.
Its ulna was approximately twice as thick as its radius.
Seven advanced embryos were found during the 1971 expedition, including two skeletons in the Khermeen Tsav redbeds.
Evidence suggests the species had superprecocial development, allowing it to fly immediately upon hatching.
The first specimens were discovered in 1971 during a Polish-Mongolian expedition to the Gobi Desert.
Fossils were first found in the Lower Nemegt Beds of the Barun Goyot Formation in the Nemegt Basin.
A species named Nanantius valifanovi was later identified as a misidentified specimen of Gobipteryx minuta.
The near-complete ossification of forelimbs and shoulders in advanced embryos supports the theory that Gobipteryx could fly at hatching.
Growth in G. minuta slowed immediately after hatching, suggesting high mobility focused energy on locomotion.
Gobipteryx was reclassified as an enantiornithes bird in 1981 after Dr. Cyril Walker defined that clade.
Gobipteryx lived during the Campanian Age of the Late Cretaceous Period.
Gobipteryx fossils date from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
